mainTopic: End of פרק כל כתבי (a גוי's light on שבת), and the start of פרק כל הכלים (moving כלים, their doors, and work tools on שבת)
overview: The amud opens by finishing the topic of light that a גוי lit on שבת. A lamp lit at a mixed gathering is lit for the majority, and שמואל turned back toward a lamp once he saw that the גוי had lit it for himself. After the הדרן for פרק כל כתבי, a new chapter begins with a משנה: all כלים and their doors may be moved on שבת, and work tools may be taken for permitted uses with food or for a child. The גמרא first asks whether doors that came off on שבת or on a weekday are the harder case. אביי rereads the משנה as speaking about doors that came off during the week. A ברייתא then allows removing a chest door but not putting it back. אביי and רבא argue about whether בנין and סתירה apply to כלים, and רבא concludes that putting the door back is forbidden only because of a גזירה שמא יתקע. Finally, רב יהודה and רבה argue about which hammer the משנה means, which raises the question of moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. רבה's reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A lamp at a gathering is lit for the majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a lamp lit at a mixed gathering follows the majority of the people there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They light it with the majority in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion that began on the previous amud. It explains that a lamp lit for a group is lit for the majority of the people there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a lamp at a gathering depends on who most of the people are. If most are גוים, we assume the lamp was lit for גוים, so a Jew may use its light. The reason is that people light a lamp for the main crowd, not for the few.

keyTerms.meaning: with the intention of / with in mind

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea for the rest of this passage: what matters is the intention of the גוי, meaning for whom he lit the light.

phrases.english: They kindle it with the majority in mind.
phrases.notes: This completes an earlier discussion: when most people at a gathering are גוים, a Jew may use the light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation earlier about lamps lit at mixed gatherings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the majority rule: the lighter's intention follows the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lamp lit for a group is considered lit for the majority of that group.

steps.title: שמואל turns away from a lamp lit by a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: שמואל visits a house, a גוי lights a lamp, and שמואל turns his face away from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל came to the house of אבי תורן. A certain גוי came and lit a lamp. שמואל turned his face away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about שמואל to show the rule in real life. This is the setup: at first, שמואל refuses to benefit from the light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew may not benefit from a מלאכה that a גוי did for a Jew on שבת. שמואל was a guest, so at first he worried that the גוי lit the lamp for him. So he turned away so as not to enjoy the light.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל did not turn away because the light itself is forbidden. He turned away because he feared it was lit for him, the Jewish guest.

phrases.english: Shmuel happened to come to the house of Avi Toran.
A certain non-Jew came and lit a lamp.
Shmuel turned his face away.
phrases.notes: He did this to avoid benefiting from the light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the 'intention of the lighter' idea through a real story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unclear whether a גוי lit a lamp for a Jew, a Jew should avoid benefiting from it.

steps.title: שמואל turns back once he sees the non-Jew lit it for himself
steps.stepSummary: When שמואל sees the גוי reading a document by the light, he concludes the lamp was lit for the גוי himself, and he turns back toward it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that the גוי brought a document and was reading it, he said: He lit it for himself. Then שמואל turned his face back toward the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with שמואל changing his mind. The גוי's reading showed that the lamp was lit for the גוי's own needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is clear the גוי lit the lamp for himself, the Jew is not benefiting from a מלאכה done for him. So the light becomes permitted. The behavior of the גוי proves his intention.

keyTerms.meaning: for his own sake / with himself in mind

steps.whatToRemember: If a גוי lights a lamp on שבת for himself, a Jew may use its light. If he lights it for a Jew, the Jew may not. We judge his intention by the facts: who most of the people are, or what the גוי actually does with the light.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁטָר וְקָא קָרֵי,
phrases.english: When he saw that he brought a document and was reading it,
he said: He lit it with himself in mind.
He turned his face back toward the lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁטָר וְקָא קָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 2 with שמואל's change of mind.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Light that a גוי clearly lit for his own use is permitted to a Jew on שבת.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter כל כתבי
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק כל כתבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל כתבי.
steps.whatsHappening: This marks the end of the chapter called כל כתבי. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a chapter. It expresses the hope to come back and learn the chapter again. The discussion of using a גוי's light ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kol Kitvei (the chapter 'All Holy Writings').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that steps 1 to 3 concluded.

steps.title: All vessels and their doors may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that all כלים may be moved on שבת, together with their doors, even doors that came off on שבת, unlike house doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All כלים may be moved on שבת, and their doors along with them, even if the doors came off on שבת. They are not like the doors of a house, because house doors are not מוכן (prepared for use).
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about moving objects on שבת. It says that any כלי, and even its removed door, may be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The door of a chest or cabinet is part of a כלי. So even if it falls off on שבת, it keeps the status of a כלי and may be moved. A house door is different: it belongs to a building, not to a כלי. It was never set aside for use on שבת, so it is מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: prepared / set aside for use (not מוקצה)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'שאינן מן המוכן' describes the house doors, not the doors of the כלים. House doors are the ones that are not מוכן. The doors of the כלים are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the chapter's main topic: which objects count as usable כלים (and may be moved), and which are מוקצה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All vessels may be moved on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The first words, כל הכלים, are the name of the new chapter.

phrases.english: and their doors along with them,
phrases.notes: For example, the doors of a chest or cabinet.

phrases.english: even if they were removed on Shabbat.
For they are not like the doors of the house,
because those (house doors) are not prepared for use.
phrases.notes: House doors belong to the building and are מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All כלים and their doors may be moved on שבת, even if the doors came off on שבת. House doors may not be moved, because they are not מוכן.

steps.title: Moving work tools to use on food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists work tools that may be moved on שבת when they are used on food: a hammer for nuts, an axe for a fig cake, a saw for cheese, and a shovel for dried figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may take a hammer to crack nuts with it, an axe to cut a pressed fig cake with it, a saw to cut cheese with it, and a shovel to scoop up dried figs with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by listing examples of heavy work tools that a person may pick up on שבת to do something permitted with food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hammers, axes, saws and shovels are usually used for work that is forbidden on שבת, yet the משנה lets a person take them for a permitted job with food. The גמרא later debates what this means. רב יהודה says the משנה means a tool set aside for the food job, such as a nut-hammer (steps 17–18). רבה says it means even a regular work tool, such as a blacksmith's hammer (steps 19–20).
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the basis for the dispute between רב יהודה and רבה about whether a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved for a permitted use (steps 17–20).

phrases.english: A person may take a hammer
to crack nuts with it,
an axe, to cut a fig cake with it.
A saw, to cut cheese with it.
A shovel, to scoop dried figs with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה by giving practical examples of moving כלים on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work tools may be moved on שבת to perform a permitted task with food.

steps.title: More examples of tools used in unusual ways
steps.stepSummary: The list continues: farm tools to hold food for a child, weaving tools to spear food, a sewing needle to remove a thorn, and a sack needle to open a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may take a winnowing shovel or a pitchfork to put food on it for a child. One may take a reed or a weaving shuttle to stick into food. One may take a hand needle to remove a thorn, and a sack maker's needle to open a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with tools used in ways quite different from their normal job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These examples are even further from each tool's normal job. A pitchfork becomes a plate for a child, and a weaving tool becomes a fork. Later, רבה uses the pitchfork case to argue that the משנה allows moving even a tool not set aside for the permitted use (step 19).

keyTerms.meaning: A reed or spindle used in weaving

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists work tools taken for permitted uses, some of them unusual. Whether this covers tools whose main use is forbidden is debated by רב יהודה and רבה (steps 17–20).

phrases.english: A winnowing shovel and a pitchfork
to put food on it for a child.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַכּוּשׁ וְאֶת הַכַּרְכֵּר — לִתְחוֹב בּוֹ.
phrases.english: A reed and a shuttle, to stick into food with it.

phrases.aramaic: מַחַט שֶׁל יָד — לִיטּוֹל בּוֹ אֶת הַקּוֹץ.
phrases.english: A hand needle, to remove a thorn with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל סַקָּאִים — לִפְתּוֹחַ בּוֹ אֶת הַדֶּלֶת.
phrases.english: And a sack maker's needle, to open the door with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further examples, this time of tools used in very unusual ways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even tools used in an unusual way may be moved on שבת for a permitted need.

steps.title: The גמרא reads an implication from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: vessels may be moved even if their parts came apart on שבת. It infers that parts which came apart during the week are surely allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: All vessels may be moved, even if their parts came apart on שבת. And it goes without saying that this is true if they came apart during the week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting the משנה and stating how it seems to read: coming apart on שבת is the big חידוש, so coming apart on a weekday is obviously fine. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' (אף) usually marks the harder case. That suggests the משנה sees parts that came apart on שבת as the harder case, which would make weekday parts the easy one. The next step will question this assumption.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the final reading. It is the reading the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
All vessels may be moved,
even if they came apart on Shabbat,
and it goes without saying if they came apart on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the ruling about doors that came off, from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plain reading: parts that came apart on שבת are the harder case, so weekday parts are certainly permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: the weekday case should be harder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite. Parts that came apart on שבת were still attached to their vessel when שבת began, so they were 'ready' for use. Parts that came apart during the week were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! If they came apart on שבת, they were prepared for use because they were attached to their 'parent' vessel when שבת began. If they came apart during the week, they were not prepared for use through their parent vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 8. It argues that parts which came apart during the week are actually the harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the item's status when שבת begins. A part still attached at that moment counts as part of a usable vessel, so it was 'ready' (מוכן). A part already loose since a weekday may have been just a piece with no use, so the משנה's 'even' seems to be pointing the wrong way.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared, ready for use when שבת begins (not מוקצה)
'Their father': the original vessel the part belongs to

steps.confusionAlert: 'אביהן' does not mean a person's father. It is a nickname for the main vessel that the loose part came from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge sets up אביי's re-reading of the משנה, which comes in step 10.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
on Shabbat they are prepared by virtue of their 'parent' vessel,

phrases.aramaic: בַּחוֹל אֵין מוּכָנִין עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבִיהֶן!
phrases.english: on a weekday they are not prepared by virtue of their 'parent' vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the inference made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that parts which came apart on שבת are the harder case, so weekday parts are surely permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The status of an item is set when שבת begins. Parts still attached then were 'prepared,' while parts already detached on a weekday were not. So the weekday case should be the harder one, which is the reverse of what the משנה's 'even' suggests.

steps.title: אביי rereads the משנה: parts that came apart during the week
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the קשיא by explaining that the משנה really means: vessels may be moved even if their parts came apart during the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the משנה means: All vessels may be moved on שבת, together with their doors. Even if the doors came apart during the week, they may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem from Step 9 by reading the משנה differently. He says the משנה is talking about parts that came apart during the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 the גמרא argued that parts that came apart on שבת are the easier case, because they were attached when שבת began. So the משנה's 'even' must point to the harder case. אביי says the משנה is teaching exactly that harder case: even parts that came apart during the week may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to reread or explain a text.
During the week, on a weekday

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the משנה allows moving vessel doors even if they came apart before שבת. Doors that came apart on שבת are allowed all the more.

phrases.english: Abaye said: this is what it means:
All vessels may be moved on Shabbat
and their doors along with them.
Even though they came apart during the week,
phrases.notes: Here's the key change: the משנה said 'on שבת,' but the גמרא now reads it as 'during the week.'

phrases.english: they may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by rereading the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's novelty was that parts that came apart on שבת may be moved, which implied that parts from the week are surely allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is teaching the harder case: even parts that came apart during the week may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא on removing and replacing doors of chests and chicken coops
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that doors of a chest, box, or closet may be removed but not put back on שבת, while a chicken coop door may be neither removed nor put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The door of a chest, a box, or a closet may be removed, but it may not be put back. The door of a chicken coop may not be removed and may not be put back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about taking doors off and putting them back on שבת. This starts a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up two cases. Vessel doors are treated differently in each direction: removing is allowed, putting back is not. A coop door is forbidden both ways. The גמרא will now try to understand the reasoning behind each case.

keyTerms.meaning: A chest, a large wooden box
They may put back, return to its place

steps.confusionAlert: Here נוֹטְלִין means taking the door off its hinges. It does not mean moving it around, which is how ניטלין was used in the משנה.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The door of a chest,
or of a box, or of a closet:
one may remove it, but one may not put it back.
And the door of a chicken coop:
one may neither remove it nor put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about removing and replacing doors, related to the משנה's theme of vessel doors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessel doors may be removed but not replaced on שבת. A chicken coop door may be neither removed nor replaced.

steps.title: The coop ruling makes sense, but what about the chest, box, and closet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the coop ruling because the coop is attached to the ground. It then asks what the ברייתא holds about vessel doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the chicken coop. The תנא holds that since it is attached to the ground, building applies to the ground and taking apart applies to the ground. But what does he hold about the chest, the box, and the closet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the coop door is forbidden both ways. Then it begins a question about the vessel doors. This line sets up the full difficulty in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coop is attached to the ground, and anything attached to the ground follows the rules of בנין and סתירה. So both removing and replacing its door are forbidden, and that is consistent. The vessel ruling is lopsided, though, so the גמרא asks what principle could explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (the first case is fine, but the second is a problem)
He holds, he is of the opinion
They are attached to the ground
Building, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת
Taking apart or demolishing, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding a chicken coop:
he holds: since it is attached to the ground,
there is building with the ground
and there is taking apart with the ground.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁל שִׁידָּה וְשֶׁל תֵּיבָה וְשֶׁל מִגְדָּל,
phrases.english: But regarding a chest, a box, and a closet,
what does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from Step 11 and accepts its coop ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling on doors of a chest, box, and closet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The coop ruling is explained by the rule that attachment to the ground brings בנין and סתירה. No clear principle yet explains the vessel ruling.

steps.title: Building and taking apart should go together for vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the difficulty: if building applies to vessels, taking apart should too, and if taking apart does not, building should not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds that building applies to vessels, then taking apart should also apply to vessels. And if taking apart does not apply to vessels, then building should not apply to vessels either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the full contradiction in the ברייתא's ruling on vessel doors. אביי answers in step 14, and רבא answers in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בנין and סתירה are a pair, so they should apply to vessels together or not at all. If both apply, removing the door should be forbidden. If neither applies, putting it back should be allowed. The ברייתא allows removing but forbids putting back, and that seems to split the pair.

keyTerms.meaning: If (used to present one side of a dilemma)
Taking apart does not apply to vessels

steps.whyThisMatters: This step relies on a basic principle: בנין and סתירה are mirror images and should go together. The answer will show how the ברייתא keeps that principle.

phrases.english: If he holds there is building with vessels,
then there is taking apart with vessels,
phrases.notes: So removing the door should be forbidden.

phrases.english: and if there is no taking apart with vessels,
then there is no building with vessels?
phrases.notes: So putting the door back should be allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in Step 12 by presenting the dilemma
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule: vessel doors may be removed but not replaced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בנין and סתירה must apply to vessels together. Either way, the ברייתא's split ruling, where removing is allowed but replacing is forbidden, contradicts itself.

steps.title: אביי rereads the ברייתא as talking about doors that already came off
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא holds building and taking apart do apply to vessels. Its wording should be read as 'doors that were already removed,' not 'one may remove doors.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the ברייתא holds that building applies to vessels and taking apart applies to vessels. When it says 'removed,' it means doors that were already removed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the difficulty from Step 13. He keeps both rules strict and changes how we read the word 'ניטלין.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If taking apart applies to vessels, then removing a door on שבת should be forbidden. To avoid that problem, אביי says the ברייתא never permitted taking the door off. It is only talking about a door that is already off. Such a door may be handled, but it may not be put back, because putting it back is building.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (used to keep an original position while answering a challenge)
The prohibition of building as it applies to vessels
The prohibition of taking apart as it applies to vessels
It means 'those that were already removed'

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Really, he (the tanna) holds
there is building with vessels
and there is dismantling with vessels,
and he means 'those that were (already) removed.'
phrases.notes: So the ברייתא is now read as talking about doors that already came off, which may be moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the consistency challenge of Step 13 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows taking doors off on שבת, which would contradict סתירה בכלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only speaks about doors already off. Both building and taking apart apply to vessels.

steps.title: רבא gives two textual objections to אביי's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the ברייתא says 'ניטלין' (one may remove), not 'that were removed.' He also points out that the word 'אבל' (but) only makes sense if the first half permits removing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: There are two answers against this. First, the ברייתא says 'they may be removed.' Second, what would 'but they may not be put back' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's rereading using the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ניטלין' plainly means 'one may remove them,' not 'ones that were already removed.' The word 'אבל' sets up a contrast: removing is allowed, but putting back is not. In אביי's reading there is no real contrast, so 'אבל' would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this point
But one may not put them back

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
There are two refutations of the matter.
One, it teaches 'they may be removed,'
phrases.notes: This is an active permission, not a description of doors already off.

phrases.english: And furthermore: what is 'but one may not put back'?
phrases.notes: The word 'but' only makes sense if removing the door was something you're allowed to do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's reinterpretation from Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain wording ('ניטלין') and the contrast word ('אבל') both show that the ברייתא permits removing the doors on שבת.

steps.title: רבא: no building or taking apart with vessels, and returning is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא holds building and taking apart do not apply to vessels. Putting the door back is forbidden only because of a decree, in case one hammers it in firmly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: He holds there is no building with vessels and no taking apart with vessels. Putting back is forbidden as a decree, in case one fixes it in firmly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the difficulty from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since taking apart does not apply to vessels, removing the door is fully allowed. By Torah law, putting it back loosely is also not building. However, the רבנן forbade putting it back so that a person will not hammer it in tightly, which would be a real מלאכה. This keeps the ברייתא consistent: the difference between removing and returning comes from a rabbinic גזירה, not from Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the previous answer and offering a new one)
Building does not apply to vessels
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a real violation
Lest he fix it in firmly

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, there is no בנין or סתירה with vessels. Removing a door of a chest is allowed, and putting it back is forbidden only because of the גזירה שמא יתקע.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: he holds:
there is no building with vessels
and there is no dismantling with vessels —
and (returning is forbidden as) a decree lest he fix it firmly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי, רבא offers a new resolution to Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New underlying position plus a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between removing and returning shows that building applies to vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither building nor taking apart applies to vessels. Returning is forbidden only by a גזירה in case he hammers it in.

steps.title: רב יהודה limits the hammer in the משנה to a nut-hammer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a person may take a hammer. רב יהודה says this means a hammer made for cracking nuts, not a blacksmith's hammer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A person may take a hammer, etc. רב יהודה said: This means a nut-hammer, used to crack nuts. But a blacksmith's hammer may not be taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רב יהודה explains which hammer the משנה allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows taking a hammer on שבת to crack nuts. רב יהודה narrows this to a hammer whose normal job is cracking nuts, which is a permitted use. A blacksmith's hammer, whose normal use is forbidden work, may not be handled even to crack nuts.

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) A person may take a hammer, etc.
Rav Yehuda said:
a hammer for nuts
to crack nuts with it,
but (a hammer) of blacksmiths — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹטֵל אָדָם קוּרְנָס כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a nut-hammer may be taken to crack nuts. A blacksmith's hammer may not.

steps.title: Why רב יהודה forbids the blacksmith's hammer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב יהודה holds an object whose main use is forbidden may not be handled, even to use it for a permitted purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that an object whose work is for a forbidden purpose may not be handled, even when it is needed for its own use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב יהודה's ruling. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blacksmith's hammer is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור, a tool mainly used for forbidden work. Some hold that such a tool may be moved לצורך גופו, meaning to use it for a permitted task. According to רב יהודה, the תנא of our משנה does not accept this leniency, so cracking nuts with a blacksmith's hammer is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An object whose main use is forbidden on שבת
For the need of the object itself (using it for a permitted task)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'לצורך גופו' with 'for the person's body.' Here it means using the tool itself for a permitted job, like cracking nuts.

phrases.english: He holds: an object whose work is for a prohibited purpose,
even for the need of its own use — is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the general principle behind רב יהודה's ruling in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יהודה, a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may not be moved even לצורך גופו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is what רבה will challenge next, and it ties into the larger מוקצה discussion of this פרק.

steps.title: רבה challenges רב יהודה from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that the end of the משנה permits a winnowing shovel and a pitchfork for a child. Those tools are never made for children, so the משנה cannot hold רב יהודה's strict view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: If that is so, look at the later part of the משנה, which says one may take a winnowing shovel and a pitchfork to put something on it for a child. Are a shovel and a pitchfork made specially for a child?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב יהודה's explanation by pointing to the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said only a tool made for a permitted use may be moved. But the end of the משנה permits a רחת and a מלגז, which are farm tools made for forbidden work, and they are being used for a permitted purpose: serving a child. So the משנה must allow moving a forbidden-use tool for a permitted need, and this goes against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But now, if so' — introduces a problem that follows from the previous claim
The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
Designate / set aside for a specific use

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the shovel is a child's toy. His point is the reverse: it is clearly NOT made for children, yet the משנה still allows using it for a child.

phrases.english: Rabbah said to him:
But now, if so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
and the winnowing shovel and the pitchfork
phrases.notes: Both are farm tools whose main use is forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: to place something on it for a child,

phrases.aramaic: רַחַת וּמַלְגֵּז מִי מְיַיחֲדִי לֵיהּ לְקָטָן?!
phrases.english: are a shovel and a pitchfork designated for a child?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's reading and the principle explained in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that the hammer must be one made for nuts, because forbidden-use tools may not be moved even for permitted needs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא permits farm tools that are never designated for children, so the משנה allows forbidden-use tools for permitted purposes. That contradicts רב יהודה's principle.

steps.title: רבה's reading: a blacksmith's hammer used to crack nuts
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the משנה means an ordinary blacksmith's hammer, taken in order to crack nuts. He then starts to explain the reasoning ('he holds…').
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: it means a blacksmiths' hammer, taken to crack nuts with it. For the תנא holds:
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב יהודה's reading, רבה gives his own explanation of the hammer in the משנה. The last word, 'קסבר', is a setup: it begins the explanation of the reasoning, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the משנה is about a real work tool, a blacksmith's hammer, being moved for a permitted use like cracking nuts. This matches the סיפא about the shovel and pitchfork. The underlying principle, that a tool whose main use is forbidden may be moved for a permitted purpose, is spelled out right after 'קסבר'.

keyTerms.meaning: A blacksmiths' hammer, a heavy work tool
'He holds' — introduces the reasoning behind a view

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous rule of כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור: according to רבה, such a tool may be moved when you need it for a permitted use.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbah said:
a blacksmiths' hammer
phrases.notes: An ordinary heavy work tool, not one specially made for nuts.

phrases.english: to crack nuts with it,
for he (the תנא) holds:
phrases.notes: Opens the explanation of the principle, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 19, רבה replaces רב יהודה's reading with his own.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה: the hammer is a nut-cracking hammer, because forbidden-use tools may not be moved.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה: the hammer is a blacksmith's hammer moved for a permitted use (cracking nuts), which fits the סיפא.
